mechanism_narrative: The observed week-on-week increase in RETAIL_REC mobility over the last two weeks (from -16.4% to -14.9%) indicates a nascent recovery trend that is likely to persist, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks as consumer confidence slowly returns.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean of the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility, currently at -21.3%, rises by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week, it will signal a significant return to office-based work, directly increasing foot traffic and boosting RETAIL_REC in urban areas over the subsequent two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the two weeks following a week-on-week rise in WORKPLACES exceeding 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained high and slightly increasing RESIDENTIAL mobility (currently 4.0%) indicates a continued preference for staying home, which directly limits out-of-home activities and will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks due to reduced overall public movement.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than the mean of the last 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent and sustained upward trend in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility over two consecutive weeks will indicate a strong return to daily commuting, synergistically boosting RETAIL_REC in urban centers over the subsequent four weeks as more people are out and about.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both rise for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days even when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show a sustained upward trend for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a period where GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable (e.g., between 5% and 10%), a significant week-on-week drop in PARKS mobility (e.g., >5 points) suggests a shift away from outdoor leisure, potentially redirecting activity towards indoor retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls > 5 points week-on-week AND GROCERY_PHARM is between 5% and 10%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases or remains stable in the week following a significant drop in PARKS, despite stable GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility remains suppressed below -20% for two consecutive weeks, it signals persistent work-from-home policies or strong recommendations, which will continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks due to reduced weekday foot traffic.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -20% for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, despite WORKPLACES remaining below -20% for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PARKS mobility (e.g., >10 percentage points week-on-week, as seen from t-1w to t-0w where it rose from -7.1% to 7.6%) indicates a strong preference for outdoor activities, which will divert leisure spending and reduce RETAIL_REC over the subsequent two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases or remains stable in the two weeks following a >10 percentage point rise in PARKS.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining above 3% and TRANSIT mobility staying below -10% for two consecutive weeks indicates a strong and persistent preference for staying home and avoiding public transport, creating a combined negative pressure that will keep RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 3% AND TRANSIT < -10% for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days, despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 3% and TRANSIT staying below -10% for two consecutive weeks.
